transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Everest Head of ML), Marcus Diaz (Platform Eng), Priya Rao (Security)

Auto Summary: POC scoping focused on cost/unit economics for a conversational scoring pipeline. Agreement to run benchmarks, share cost model spreadsheet, and validate security/compliance assets prior to POC kickoff.

[00:00] Jenna Park: Great, thanks everyone for joining. quick intro, i'm jenna park, AE on the account, with samir from our se team. today we want to nail down success criteria, traffic profile, and a rough cost model so we can scope a 4-week poc.
[00:22] Laura Chen: Thanks, jenna. quick context, at Everest we run a question-answer scoring service for loan underwriting — about 4M daily requests, peaks at 600 rps, average payload ~1.2k tokens, scoring + follow-up generation combined. main goals are latency under 200ms p95 for scoring, and keep incremental cost under $0.02 per user in production.
[00:48] Samir Patel: ok, helpful. when you say scoring + generation, is scoring a short prompt (200-400 tokens) and generation longer?
[00:58] Laura Chen: yes scoring ~300 tokens avg, generation when triggered is around 1.2k tokens but that's less frequent, maybe 12% of requests.
[01:12] Marcus Diaz: i can add we run this in a hybrid cloud; we need a VPC/private option for any PII flows. latency to our region is a factor — we've seen 50-60ms network hops to typical cloud endpoints.
[01:28] Priya Rao: and from security, we'll need SOC2 artifacts, SSO/SAML, RBAC and KMS/HSM support. encryption at rest + in transit is mandatory.
[01:40] Jenna Park: totally, we can include our SOC2 pack and KMS integration notes. high-level cost questions first — can you confirm monthly token volume and desired budget?
[01:52] Laura Chen: roughly 120M tokens/day across scoring + gen, so say 3.6B tokens/month. Budget we're evaluating is around $40k/mo for inference initially, can stretch if latency gains justify it.
[02:06] Samir Patel: ok so rough calc: for hosted, per-token price for a mid-sized LLM varies — our default open-model hosted SKU sits at approx $0.0008 per token for generation-equivalent tokens, embeddings are different but not relevant here. for 3.6B tokens that would be ~ $2.88M — that can't be right, wait i misread — double check units. actually at $0.0008 per 1k tokens? sorry let me reframe — typical hosted API numbers are in $/1k tokens. Jenna?
[02:42] Jenna Park: yeah sorry common confusion. our pricing quotes are per 1k input+output tokens. for reference, hosted open model baseline is $0.80 per 1k tokens for the LLM family we discussed; dedicated reserved capacity changes that math dramatically.
[02:58] Laura Chen: ah ok that lines up better. so 3.6B tokens/month at $0.80 per 1k tokens = $2,880,000 — still huge. so we need to lean into dedicated or heavy caching/batching.
[03:12] Samir Patel: exactly. two levers: 1) Dedicated/reserved capacity reduces unit cost substantially — think 5-20x lower depending on model and commit. 2) caching + batching reduce effective tokens sent to model; prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts can lower tokens by 30-70% depending on reuse.
[03:28] Marcus Diaz: can you give a concrete example of 'effective tokens' after caching?
[03:34] Samir Patel: if your scoring uses a standard prompt with only a variable section (customer data), prefix caching could save the model from re-evaluating the static prompt. in practice for scoring we've seen effective token reduction to about 60% of raw tokens if your prefix reuse is high. so from 3.6B raw tokens you might only send ~2.2B effective tokens. also batching reduces per-request overhead and increases throughput but doesn't change token count — it reduces cost per request by improving GPU utilization when on dedicated.
[04:00] Jenna Park: to be safe we'll model both: optimistic cache hit 50% and conservative 20%, and two capacity modes: dedicated reserved and hosted.
[04:12] Laura Chen: what's the typical dedicated per-1k-token number?
[04:16] Samir Patel: ballpark, dedicated (reserved) for a conv model on A100-class or similar quantized stack can get to $0.05-0.12 per 1k tokens depending on commit and quantization (INT8/4). that's orders of magnitude better than hosted list. plus better p95 latency.
[04:34] Laura Chen: okay that sits closer to our $40k/mo target if we can get effective tokens down. e.g., 2.2B tokens /1k * $0.08 = $176,000 — still high. we need to look at batching and skipping generation when possible.
[04:50] Samir Patel: two more knobs — response truncation and early exit heuristics, and model variant routing: you can route lower-confidence requests to a smaller, cheaper model. That can reduce average cost per request by 20-40% if accuracy budget allows.
[05:10] Marcus Diaz: latency targets: scoring under 200ms p95, generation can be relaxed to 500ms p95. what SLOs can you guarantee on dedicated?
[05:20] Jenna Park: our dedicated SLA targets are configurable but typical p95 goals for scoring-class workloads are under 150-200ms when pinned to a GPU pool with correct batching. we will include benchmark runs to validate.
[05:34] Priya Rao: procurement question — do you handle key management or do we manage keys in our KMS?
[05:40] Samir Patel: customer-managed KMS is supported; we integrate with common cloud KMS services and HSMs. we can do encrypted KV cache and audit logs for requests.
[05:50] Laura Chen: great. on benchmarks — what exactly do you want from our side to run a realistic test?
[05:56] Samir Patel: we need sample traffic pattern: rps distribution, payload sizes for scoring and generation, and golden prompt set for quality checks. Marcus, you mentioned nightly batch jobs — if those are heavy we should include a tail-run in benchmarks.
[06:12] Marcus Diaz: yes we have nightly enrichment that spikes for up to 20 minutes at 1.2k rps.
[06:18] Samir Patel: ok include that. plan: 1) small smoke with 1-2 mins at target rps to validate latency, 2) longer 2-hour benchmark that mixes scoring + generation + spike, measuring p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and GPU utilization. we will provide the runbook.
[06:36] Jenna Park: for the cost model spreadsheet i'll include columns for raw tokens, effective tokens after cache%, per-1k-token price for Hosted vs Dedicated, batching assumptions (avg batch size 1.5-> 8) and routing to cheaper model percent.
[06:50] Laura Chen: can you give an example row? say conservative: 20% cache hit, 15% small-model routing, batch size 4, dedicated at $0.08/1k tokens.
[07:02] Samir Patel: sure. raw tokens 3.6B -> effective after cache 0.8 * 3.6B = 2.88B. small-model routing reduces heavy-gen weight by 15% of tokens -> call it 2.45B. per-1k tokens at $0.08 -> 2.45M * $0.08 = $196k/mo. still above target. if cache hit 50% -> effective 1.8B -> with routing -> ~1.53B -> ~ $122k/mo.
[07:36] Marcus Diaz: that's still a couple x above our $40k target. where does the biggest delta come from? is it model size or token volume?
[07:44] Samir Patel: mainly token volume. other approaches: 1) aggressive caching (increase prefix reuse), 2) increase routing to smaller models for low-risk requests, 3) push some logic to on-device or cheaper infra, 4) apply quantization to reduce dedicated cost and get steeper discounts.
[08:02] Laura Chen: acceptable risk: 40% of scoring can route to small model if we maintain >98% correlation with main model. generation route is more sensitive.
[08:12] Jenna Park: we should define success criteria concretely: a) p95 scoring latency <= 200ms in dedicated POC, b) end-to-end monthly cost <= $60k (target), c) quality regression less than 2% on golden set. Does that sound ok?
[08:28] Laura Chen: yes we can sign up to those if you can demonstrate the $60k projection in the cost model with feasible caching/routing knobs.
[08:36] Priya Rao: from security side, non-negotiables: customer-managed KMS, audit logs for every request, and data retention/auto-delete policy for training data. we also want an agreed-upon SOC2 attestation before production.
[08:52] Jenna Park: noted. we'll attach our SOC2 report and a KMS integration doc.
[08:58] Samir Patel: on the benchmark technicals: we'll run models on dedicated quantized variant (we recommend q4_int8 style) for better throughput. we'll measure token/sec per GPU and estimate cost per 1k tokens based on GPU-hour price and throughput.
[09:18] Marcus Diaz: can you walk through how you convert GPU-hour into per-1k-token?
[09:22] Samir Patel: yes short version: measure tokens/sec for a given model + sequence length, compute tokens/hour per GPU, then divide the hourly infra cost (GPU+infra amortized + ops) by tokens/hour to get $/token, then multiply by 1k. e.g., if an A100 node yields 10M tokens/hour and effective infra cost is $5/hour -> $5 / 10M = $0.0000005 per token -> $0.0005 per 1k tokens. numbers are illustrative; actuals depend on batch sizes and sequence length.

Notes on transcription: minor ASR errors: "KMS" occasionally transcribed as "K M S", "p95" sometimes as "p nine five"; proper nouns may be miscapitalized.
transcript_continued:
[10:00] Laura Chen: numbers like that look promising if we can get to 10M tokens/hour. what's realistic for our 300-token scoring vs 1.2k gen?
[10:08] Samir Patel: shorter sequences increase throughput — scoring will have much higher tokens/sec. generation with 1.2k sequences reduces tokens/sec and increases latency. so mixed workloads are the tough part; that's why routing to cheaper model for scoring is attractive.
[10:26] Jenna Park: timeline: propose 2 weeks of prep (traffic, golden prompts, security checklist), then a 2-week POC with benchmarks + one integration sprint — total 4 weeks to decision.
[10:40] Laura Chen: procurement also needs pricing commitment for dedicated — do you have a standard starter commitment?
[10:46] Jenna Park: yes we have 3-tier reserved options: monthly minimums that buy deeper unit discounts. our Sales Ops will propose a starter commit that hits mid-range discounts; i'll include that in the pricing doc.
[10:56] Marcus Diaz: regarding observability, what traces and cost attribution do you provide? we need per-route and per-model token breakdowns and token-level cost.
[11:06] Samir Patel: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, trace ids to tie back to your logs, and a route-level bill. we can also stream usage logs to your SIEM.
[11:22] Priya Rao: audit logging and retention windows matter; can we configure retention per route?
[11:26] Samir Patel: yes retention is configurable; we can align to your compliance policy during POC.
[11:33] Laura Chen: any limitations on model versions during POC? we want to test a smaller distilled variant alongside a larger baseline to check regression.
[11:40] Samir Patel: no problem; we encourage canarying. Redwood supports multi-model routing and automatic fallback if the cheaper model fails quality checks.
[11:50] Jenna Park: ok let's do a quick sketch of the benchmark matrix: (1) scoring only at 600 rps sustained, (2) mixed at 400 rps scoring + 60 rps gen, (3) spike test with nightly batch at 1.2k rps for 20 minutes. For each run measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and effective per-1k-token cost.
[12:12] Marcus Diaz: sounds good. we'll provide simulated traffic plus a small sample of live traffic if allowed.
[12:18] Laura Chen: about privacy — we will mask PII in sample data; we still need assurance that raw logs are encrypted and access is restricted.
[12:26] Priya Rao: and contractual clause around data deletion after POC.
[12:30] Jenna Park: we'll include a POC addendum with deletion & retention clauses.
[12:36] Samir Patel: on the cost model spreadsheet i'll add scenario tabs: "conservative" (20% cache hit, 10% routing), "baseline" (35% cache, 20% routing), "optimistic" (50% cache, 35% routing). each will compute monthly cost for hosted vs dedicated and show the break-even commit size.
[12:58] Laura Chen: can you also model the impact of batch size? we saw 2x throughput improvement moving from avg batch 2 to avg batch 6 in prior tests.
[13:06] Samir Patel: yes we'll include batch sensitivity analysis. batching helps more on dedicated where you control queuing; hosted has limits due to latency SLOs.
[13:16] Marcus Diaz: any caveats for our hybrid deployment? we want the control plane in your hosted service but the inference in our VPC.
[13:24] Jenna Park: Redwood Private supports a customer-managed inference plane with control plane tie-in; we'll map the network flow and outline egress rules. we'll include a diagram in the docs.
[13:36] Laura Chen: procurement will likely ask for a simple TCO comparison: current infra + naive GPU self-host vs Redwood Dedicated vs hosted. can you help prepare that?
[13:44] Jenna Park: yes, the cost-model spreadsheet will include a self-host column using your provided GPU-hour pricing. that will help procurement.
[13:52] Priya Rao: if we go with dedicated, what's the typical onboarding time? we have some internal deadlines mid-February.
[13:58] Jenna Park: dedicated onboarding is typically 2-4 weeks once commit and network peering are set. so mid-February is plausible if we kickoff POC now and decide by mid-January.
[14:10] Laura Chen: ok timeline works. any initial blockers?
[14:14] Marcus Diaz: we need clarity on egress costs and whether the metrics we collect will include GPU-level attribution for chargeback.
[14:22] Samir Patel: egress depends on your cloud; we'll model it separately. GPU attribution is part of our Console usage exports.
[14:30] Jenna Park: let's recap next steps: 1) Jenna sends cost-model + SOC2 + KMS doc (due 12/13), 2) Marcus provides traffic profile and sample prompts (due 12/13), 3) Samir prepares benchmark runbook and initial cluster config (due 12/14), 4) Priya reviews security docset (due 12/18), 5) schedule 2-hour benchmark (week of 12/15).
[14:52] Laura Chen: sounds good. i'm noting the success criteria again: p95 <=200ms, cost <=$60k/mo target, quality regression <2%.
[15:02] Jenna Park: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the spreadsheet.
[15:08] Meeting end
